headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: Rasa can feed unverified dialogue into Transformers, which has broad filesystem and shell powers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa ingests external chat content via messaging APIs, and Transformers can read files and run browsers/shells. If Rasa output is bridged into Transformers without sanitization, prompt-like content can steer downstream behavior. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred from their exposed I/O surfaces rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are copied into Transformers prompts or stdin without filtering, injection is plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between them, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a strict content separator and instruction/data delimiter.
Strip or escape user-authored markup before forwarding text.
Require human review for any prompt assembled from Rasa output.
Disable browser/tool execution for inputs originating from chat.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa handles text and voice, while Transformers can read and write files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files are forwarded between them, sensitive conversation data can leak into model inputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so the pathway is plausible but not confirmed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, conversation artifacts can be exposed to Transformers.
IF Transformers loads files produced by Rasa, those contents may be transmitted to external services.
mitigations: Store Rasa transcripts in a separate directory.
Remove voice/text logs before any file-based handoff.
Restrict Transformers network egress to approved endpoints.
Rotate or redact sensitive conversation logs before processing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Transformers has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities, while Rasa can operate as a multi-channel support bot. If both touch the same mutable workspace, concurrent edits or installs can corrupt files or state. Rasa does not advertise locking, and Transformers explicitly supports multiple instances, so the conflict pathway is credible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF Transformers installs packages while Rasa is running from the same environment, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Give each agent its own working directory.
Run package installs only in a separate build step.
Use file locks around any shared artifacts.
Mount shared paths read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can generate conversational outputs that may be treated as authoritative by a downstream Transformers pipeline. Transformers can then read files, run subprocesses, and act on that input without a documented verification step. That creates a classic unverified handoff where errors or hallucinations from Rasa can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or artifacts.
conditions: IF Transformers consumes Rasa-generated text as facts or instructions, errors can propagate.
IF downstream scripts act on those outputs, the blast radius includes incorrect files or commands.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action.
Require schema validation on Rasa outputs.
Log and diff all transformed outputs before execution.
Limit Transformers to read-only analysis for Rasa content.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and human approval.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa is a customer-support agent handling text and voice, while Transformers processes multimodal data and can write files and use broad egress. If support conversations contain regulated personal data and are routed into Transformers without a DPA or retention controls, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF support transcripts include regulated personal data, compliance review is required.
IF Transformers stores or forwards those transcripts, retention and residency controls must be checked.
mitigations: Classify the data before any handoff.
Redact personal data from support transcripts.
Set explicit retention limits for both agents.
Restrict outbound destinations for Transformers.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA coverage.
